title: Chapter 9: Advent of Europeans in India

blocks.content: The arrival of Europeans in India marked the beginning of a new phase in Indian history. European traders came to India in search of spices, silk, cotton, and other valuable goods. Gradually, trade turned into political control.
1. Background: Why Europeans Came to India

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Vasco da Gama discovered the direct sea route to India, arriving at Calicut in 1498 where he was received by King Zamorin.
The Portuguese were the first European power to arrive in India (1498) and the last to leave (1961 from Goa).
The English East India Company was granted a trading charter by Queen Elizabeth I in 1600, opening its first factory at Surat in 1613.
The Dutch established their primary early factory at Masulipatnam in 1605 but were ousted by the British following the Battle of Bedara (1759).
The French established their headquarters at Pondicherry under François Martin.
The Anglo-French Rivalry culminated in three Carnatic Wars, ultimately establishing British dominance in India.

blocks.content: • India was famous for spices, textiles, silk and precious stones.
• European countries wanted direct trade with India.
• The traditional trade routes were controlled by Arabs and Turks.
• The discovery of sea routes made direct trade possible.
2. Discovery of Sea Route to India
3. Portuguese in India
• The Portuguese were the first Europeans to establish trading posts in India.
• Francisco de Almeida became the first Governor of Portuguese India.
• Afonso de Albuquerque captured Goa in 1510 and made it the capital of Portuguese India.
• The Portuguese introduced tobacco and printing press in India.
4. Dutch in India
• The Dutch East India Company was established in 1602.
• The Dutch established trading centers in Surat, Pulicat, Nagapattinam and Cochin.
• They mainly traded in spices.
• They were defeated by the British in the Battle of Bedara (1759).
5. English (British) in India
• The English East India Company was established in 1600.
• The first English factory in India was established at Surat in 1613.
• Sir Thomas Roe visited the court of Mughal emperor Jahangir.
• The British gradually expanded their political power in India.
6. French in India
• The French East India Company was established in 1664.
• They established trading centers at Pondicherry, Chandernagore, Mahe and Karaikal.
• Dupleix was the most famous French governor in India.
• The French and British fought the Carnatic Wars.
7. Anglo-French Rivalry (Carnatic Wars)
8. Impact of European Arrival
• Expansion of trade and commerce.
• Introduction of new goods and technologies.
• Beginning of European political influence in India.

items: Chronological Sequence of Arrival: Portuguese (1498) -> Dutch (1602) -> English (1608) -> Danish (1616) -> French (1664).
Alfonso de Albuquerque is known as the real founder of Portuguese power in India after capturing Goa from the Sultan of Bijapur in 1510.
Battle of Bedara (1759): The English crushed Dutch power in India.
Battle of Wandiwash (1760): British General Eyre Coote defeated French commander Count de Lally, ending French territorial ambitions in India.

blocks.content: • Rise of British dominance in India.
SSC Exam Important Facts
• Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in 1498.
• Portuguese were the first Europeans to come to India.
• English East India Company was established in 1600.
• Sir Thomas Roe visited Jahangir's court.
• British defeated the French in the Carnatic Wars.
